findings.title: The feed's empty state ("No moves yet") is rendered from a Pittsburgh-fallback query that runs before GPS resolves
findings.location: src/hooks/useNearbyMoves.ts:34-56 (no `enabled`, `const { lat, lng } = coords ?? PITTSBURGH` at :43) + src/components/feed/FeedList.tsx:39-45 and :61
findings.reproduction: Cold start on a device outside Pittsburgh. `useLocationStore.coords` starts null (src/store/locationStore.ts:18) and `useLocationInit` only fills it after the permission dialog plus `getCurrentPositionAsync({accuracy: Balanced})` returns — seconds indoors. Tap the Feed tab during that window: useNearbyMoves fires `nearby_moves` against PITTSBURGH (40.4406,-79.9959). nearby_moves also filters `starts_at >= now() and <= now() + 24h` (supabase/migrations/016_one_nearby_moves.sql:122-126), so for a non-Pittsburgh user it returns []. isLoading goes false, `moves` is [], and FeedList renders ListEmptyComponent. When coords then resolve, the queryKey changes (:46) and `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` (:55) re-serves the previous *empty* pages — query-core sets status='success', so isLoading stays false and the same empty state is still on screen through the second fetch. The same happens on the third key change when `uid` resolves from authStore, and on any FilterBar category/radius tap whose previous result was empty.
findings.consequence: A first-time user's first look at the core feed says "No moves yet — Be the first to set the move for today" on a night when there are moves two blocks away. It is not a flicker: it persists for the whole GPS acquisition plus the refetch, and it is indistinguishable from a genuine empty city. Users who tap a category filter that has no cached page get the same message instead of skeletons.
findings.fix: Don't query the fallback until the location attempt has settled, and treat placeholder data as loading. (1) src/store/locationStore.ts: add `resolved: false` and `setResolved: (resolved) => set({ resolved })`. (2) src/hooks/useLocation.ts requestLocation(): wrap the body in `try { ... } finally { setFetching(false); useLocationStore.getState().setResolved(true); }` so a GPS/permission throw still settles it. (3) src/hooks/useNearbyMoves.ts: `const resolved = useLocationStore((s) => s.resolved);` and add `enabled: resolved` to the useInfiniteQuery — the Pittsburgh fallback then only serves the deliberate permission-denied case that list.tsx:50 already advertises. (4) src/components/feed/FeedList.tsx:21 and :39: destructure `isPending, isPlaceholderData` and change the guard to `if (isPending || isPlaceholderData) { return <skeletons/> }` — isPending is true while the query is disabled and while a new key is in flight behind placeholder data, so the empty state can only render on a settled, real result.

findings.title: "See all" attendees screen renders a blank list and a "(0)" header while loading — isLoading is destructured and never used

findings.reproduction: Open any move with more than 6 attendees, tap "See all" (app/move/[id].tsx:225). findings.title: Map's Spots layer spins forever when nearby_spots fails — the loading flag is never cleared on the throw path
findings.location: app/(tabs)/index.tsx:66-84 (fetchLayer: `setIsLoading(false)` only at :83, after an unguarded await) and :87-91, :95-100, :102-106 (three call sites, none with a .catch); src/hooks/useSpots.ts:26 (`if (error) throw error`)
findings.reproduction: Tap "📍 Spots" on the map with the network down (or any condition where the nearby_spots RPC returns an error — postgrest-js converts a failed fetch into `{ error }`). The layer effect at :87-91 sets isLoading true, fetchLayer awaits fetchNearbySpots, which throws, so line 83 never runs and the rejection is unhandled.
findings.consequence: The user sits on a pin-less map with the orange spinner at :284-288 pinned at 48% height indefinitely — no error, no retry control, no empty state. It only clears if they pan the map (which re-triggers fetchLayer via the debounce) or switch back to Moves. The Moves branch has the inverse defect: :71-78 destructures only `data` and ignores `error`, so a failed request calls `setMoves([])` and the map confidently reports "No moves in view" (:268-282).
findings.fix: Give fetchLayer a settled path and an error flag: wrap the body in `try { ... } catch (e) { setLoadError(true); } finally { setIsLoading(false); }`, and in the moves branch destructure `const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc(...)` and `if (error) throw error;` so both layers take the same path. Render `loadError` as a tappable "Couldn't load — tap to retry" card in place of the empty-state card at :268, clearing it at the top of fetchLayer. Separately, add `setIsLoading(true)` inside onRegionChangeComplete's timeout at :105 so a pan out of an empty area doesn't keep "No moves in view" on screen while the next region loads.

findings.title: Move and Spot detail screens render the shimmer skeleton permanently when the query errors
findings.reproduction: Open a move or spot whose row is gone or unreadable — a shared link to a deleted move, or a spot whose `get_spot` returns no row (src/hooks/useSpots.ts:36 throws 'spot_not_found'). After the two default retries (src/lib/queryClient.ts:8-9, ~6s), status is 'error': isLoading is false and data is undefined, so the guard's `!move` / `!spot` arm keeps rendering the same Skeleton block forever.
findings.consequence: The screen shimmers indefinitely, promising content that will never arrive, and the skeleton branch renders no back button — the user has to guess at the OS back gesture. R9 \u2014 TOUCH TARGETS.scanned: Read all 23 files in /home/user/wtm/wtm/app and all 12 component files in /home/user/wtm/wtm/src that contain onPress/Pressable/TouchableOpacity/TouchableHighlight/Button (grep found zero Pressable, zero TouchableHighlight, zero RN <Button> — every control in this app is a TouchableOpacity or an Animated TouchableOpacity). For each of the 71 interactive elements I computed the rendered box from its own style: explicit width/height where given, otherwise padding*2 + content box (Ionicons render as a Text glyph of exactly `size` pt; label Text with no lineHeight override renders at ~1.2*fontSize on both iOS SF Pro and Android Roboto) + borderWidth*2. I also grepped the whole tree for `hitSlop` (exactly ONE occurrence, app/user/[id].tsx:159) and `pressRetentionOffset` (zero), and grepped every `lineHeight` to confirm no button label overrides the default metric — none do; all 21 lineHeight uses are on paragraph/body text. Excluded from findings: src/components/ui/Button.tsx (its `sm` variant is h-9 = 36pt, but grep confirms the component has zero call sites and never renders), and the two RN <Switch> controls in app/(tabs)/create.tsx (native OS control, fixed 51x31 on iOS, not stylable). RESULT: NOT A PASS — 34 of 71 targets compute under 44x44pt, and the single hitSlop in the codebase only reaches 38pt.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is a bare 20pt icon with no padding and no hitSlop — 20x20pt
findings.reproduction: Cold launch → Welcome → tap "Already have an account? Sign in" → type anything into the Password field → tap the eye icon at the right edge of the password row. Same control on the sign-up path: Welcome → "I have an invite code" → enter a valid code → Validate → tap the eye icon on the PASSWORD field.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: `<TouchableOpacity onPress={...}>` at sign-in.tsx:85 carries NO style prop at all, so the touchable shrink-wraps its only child, `<Ionicons size={20}>`, which renders as a 20pt glyph — a 20x20pt target (≈20x24 including text line box). That is 45% of the 44pt minimum on the horizontal axis. It sits flush against the right inner edge of a 52pt-tall input row whose only other child is a flex:1 TextInput, so every miss lands on the TextInput and re-opens the keyboard instead of revealing the password. A user who mistyped their password gets no reliable way to check it and is pushed toward repeated failed sign-in attempts.
findings.fix:
Add hitSlop to both. 20 + 12 + 12 = 44pt exactly, and it costs no layout because the row has `gap: 8` and 16pt of paddingHorizontal to absorb it:

  <TouchableOpacity
    onPress={() => setShowPassword((s) => !s)}
    hitSlop={{ top: 12, bottom: 12, left: 12, right: 12 }}
  >
    <Ionicons name={showPassword ? 'eye-off' : 'eye'} size={20} color="#606060" />
  </TouchableOpacity>

findings.title: Every hand-rolled back/close button is a bare 24pt (or 26pt) icon with no padding — 24x24pt, and headerShown:false means it is the only visible way back
findings.location: app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx:44-46; app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx:103-105; app/(auth)/invite.tsx:67-69; app/(tabs)/profile/edit.tsx:71-73; app/move/[id]/attendees.tsx:34-36; app/user/[id].tsx:153-155; app/user/[id].tsx:123-125; app/invite-friends.tsx:51-53; app/add-spot.tsx:90-92
findings.reproduction: Any of nine routes. Most severe: Profile tab → tap "Edit" → tap the back arrow at top-left of Edit Profile. Also: Move detail → "See all" → back arrow on the attendees list; Profile → Invite friends card → back arrow; long-press the map → Drop a Spot → the X at top-left.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: each of these is `<TouchableOpacity onPress={() => router.back()}>` wrapping `<Ionicons size={24}>` with either no style or a style that sets only margin (e.g. sign-in.tsx:44 sets `marginBottom: 32`, which is outside the touch box). Margin is not padding, so the target is the glyph: 24x24pt — 55% of 44pt on both axes. add-spot.tsx:90 uses `size={26}` → 26x26pt. Both root and (auth) Stacks set `headerShown: false` (app/_layout.tsx:53, app/(auth)/_layout.tsx:6), so there is no native back chevron to fall back on. app/(tabs)/profile/edit.tsx is registered as a Tabs.Screen with `href: null` (app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:124), not a Stack screen, so there is no iOS edge-swipe-back for it either — a missed tap on that 24pt arrow strands the user on Edit Profile with no other exit. Compounding it, these arrows sit in the top-left corner where the thumb is least accurate on a one-handed grip.
findings.fix:
Add hitSlop to each (24 + 10 + 10 = 44pt; for the 26pt close in add-spot use 9). Nothing shifts, because every one of these sits in a header row with >=16pt of surrounding padding:

  <TouchableOpacity
    onPress={() => router.back()}
    hitSlop={{ top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 10, right: 10 }}
  >
    <Ionicons name="arrow-back" size={24} color="#FAFAFA" />
  </TouchableOpacity>

findings.title: Radius filter pills are 26pt tall — the smallest padded control in the app
findings.reproduction: Feed tab (or Map tab → list icon top-right) → the second horizontal pill row under the category row → tap "1 mi" / "3 mi" / "5 mi" / "10 mi" / "25 mi".
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: paddingVertical 5 * 2 = 10, plus label at fontSize 12 with no lineHeight override ≈ 14.4pt, plus borderWidth 1 * 2 = 2 → 26.4pt tall. That is 60% of 44pt, and it holds under any plausible font metric (even at 1.35x the label the total is 28pt). No hitSlop. The pill also sits inside a horizontal ScrollView, so any vertical drift during the tap is interpreted as the start of a scroll gesture and cancels the press. This control selects the search radius for the entire feed — a user trying to widen from 1mi to 25mi on an empty feed repeatedly hits nothing or scrolls the row sideways.

findings.title: Category/layer filter pills are 31-34pt tall across both the feed and the map
findings.reproduction: Map tab (the app's landing screen after auth) → tap "🕺 Moves" / "📍 Spots" in the centered segmented control under the header, then tap any emoji pill in the row below it ("🔥 All", "🍺 Bars", …). Same category pills on the Feed tab via FilterBar.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic — FilterBar.tsx:29 category pill: paddingVertical 7*2 = 14, tallest child is the emoji Text at fontSize 14 ≈ 16.8pt, plus borderWidth 1*2 = 2 (inactive) → 32.8pt; active pills set borderWidth 0 → 30.8pt. index.tsx:396 FilterPill: paddingVertical 8*2 = 16, emoji fontSize 13 ≈ 15.6, border 1*2 = 2 → 33.6pt. index.tsx:378 LayerTab: paddingVertical 8*2 = 16, label fontSize 13 ≈ 15.6, no border → 31.6pt. All 70-76% of 44pt, none with hitSlop. The map pills are worse than the feed pills because they are absolutely positioned over a live MapView: a missed tap is not a no-op — it falls through to the MapView's `onPress={clearSelection}` (index.tsx:151) or, if held, to `onLongPress` (index.tsx:152) which fires a Heavy haptic and pushes the user to /add-spot. So a fat-fingered attempt to filter the map can navigate the user to the Drop a Spot form instead.

findings.title: RSVPButton compact is 36pt tall — the primary conversion action on every feed card and every map card
findings.location: src/components/moves/RSVPButton.tsx:82 (`height: compact ? 36 : 48`), rendered compact at src/components/moves/MoveCard.tsx:207 and app/(tabs)/index.tsx:316
findings.reproduction: Feed tab → scroll the move list → tap "Join Move" on any card's footer row. Or: Map tab → tap any move pin → tap "Join Move" in the bottom card.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: explicit `height: 36` when `compact` is true — no computation needed, it is 36pt, 82% of 44. Width is fine (paddingHorizontal 14*2 + icon 15 + gap 6 + "Join Move" ≈ 104pt), so this fails on the vertical axis only. No hitSlop. This is the app's core action, and in the feed it lives inside a FlatList (`src/components/feed/FeedList.tsx:48`) where a tap with any vertical drift is claimed by the scroll responder — an 8pt-short target makes that materially more likely. On the map card (index.tsx:316) the button sits 96pt off the bottom of the screen inside a floating card, directly above the 80pt tab bar.

findings.title: Hype reaction pills are 35pt tall and 47pt wide when the count is zero
findings.reproduction: Feed tab → any move card → tap one of the emoji reaction pills in the bottom row of the card (rendered by MoveCard.tsx:212). Or: Move detail screen → the reaction row below the description (app/move/[id].tsx:216).
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: paddingVertical 7*2 = 14, tallest child is the emoji Text at fontSize 16 ≈ 19.2pt, borderWidth 1*2 = 2 → 35.2pt tall. Width when `total === 0` (the count Text is conditionally omitted at line 40): paddingHorizontal 13*2 = 26 + emoji ≈ 19 + border 2 = 47pt; the `gap: 5` contributes nothing because there is only one child. So an un-reacted pill is ≈47x35 — it fails vertically. Every move starts with all counts at zero, meaning the *first* reaction on any move is always the hardest to hit. Like the RSVP button these render inside the feed FlatList, so a short target plus scroll-responder competition means taps get swallowed.

findings.title: Header submit buttons ("Post it", "Drop it", "Save", "Edit") are 30-34pt tall
findings.reproduction: Create tab → fill in title, pick a vibe, type a location → tap "Post it" at top-right. Long-press the map → fill the form → tap "Drop it" at top-right. Profile tab → tap "Edit" at top-right → change your display name → tap "Save" at top-right.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic. create.tsx:150 "Post it": paddingVertical 8*2 = 16 + label fontSize 15 ≈ 18 → 34pt. add-spot.tsx:96 "Drop it": 8*2 = 16 + fontSize 14 ≈ 16.8 → 32.8pt. profile/edit.tsx:75 "Save": paddingVertical 7*2 = 14 + fontSize 14 ≈ 16.8 → 30.8pt. profile/index.tsx:64 "Edit": 7*2 = 14 + tallest child is the label at fontSize 13 ≈ 15.6 (the icon is only 14) → 29.6pt. None has hitSlop; all four sit in the top-right corner, the least reachable zone on a phone held one-handed. These are the terminal actions of long forms — a user who has filled out the entire Set The Move form and cannot land the 34pt commit button has no other way to submit (there is no keyboard-accessory submit and the TextInputs at create.tsx:201 and :333 are `multiline`, so Return inserts a newline rather than submitting).

findings.title: The map card dismiss (X) is 28x28pt and a miss falls through to the map underneath
findings.location: app/(tabs)/index.tsx:306-308 (selected move card) and app/(tabs)/index.tsx:339-341 (selected spot card)
findings.reproduction: Map tab → tap any move pin → the detail card slides up from the bottom → tap the X at the card's top-right to dismiss it. Same on the Spots layer: tap "📍 Spots" → tap any diamond pin → tap the X.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: `style={{ padding: 4 }}` around `<Ionicons name="close" size={20}>` → 20 + 4*2 = 28x28pt, 64% of 44. No hitSlop. The X is nested inside an outer TouchableOpacity (index.tsx:293 / :324) whose onPress navigates to `/move/${id}` or `/spot/${id}`, and it is inset at the card's top-right corner. A miss on the 28pt X therefore does not do nothing — it hits the parent and pushes a full-screen detail route the user was trying to dismiss, forcing them back out through that screen's own 40pt back button (index of this same registry, finding 10).

findings.title: Text-only links have no padding box: "See all" is 17pt tall
findings.location: app/move/[id].tsx:225-228 ("See all", ≈52x17); app/move/[id].tsx:299-320 ("Report this move", 28pt tall); app/(auth)/verify-age.tsx:181-186 ("Wrong account? Sign out", 32pt tall)
findings.reproduction: "See all": open any move with more than 6 attendees (Feed → tap a card → scroll to "Who's going") → tap "See all" at the right of that section header. "Report this move": same screen, scroll past the chat block, tap the grey "Report this move" line. "Wrong account? Sign out": sign up with a new account → the age gate appears → tap the grey line under the "Let's go 🔥" button.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic. move/[id].tsx:225 is `<TouchableOpacity onPress={...}><Text style={{fontSize: 14, fontWeight:'600'}}>See all</Text></TouchableOpacity>` with no style prop anywhere — the target is the text box: 7 glyphs ≈ 52pt wide by ≈16.8pt tall. 17pt is 38% of the 44pt minimum, the smallest target in the app. move/[id].tsx:299 "Report this move" sets only `paddingVertical: 6` → 12 + fontSize 13 ≈ 15.6 = 27.6pt. verify-age.tsx:181 sets `paddingVertical: 8` → 16 + 15.6 = 31.6pt. None has hitSlop. "See all" is the sole route to /move/[id]/attendees — there is no other entry point in the codebase — so a user on a popular move cannot reliably reach the full attendee list. "Report this move" being a 28pt target matters more than its visual weight suggests: it is the app's only in-move safety escalation path, reached by a user who has just seen something they want gone.

findings.title: Round icon buttons at 36-40pt: detail-screen back buttons, chat send, and the map/feed toggle
findings.location: app/move/[id].tsx:389-399 (40x40); app/spot/[id].tsx:253-263 (40x40); src/components/moves/MoveChat.tsx:175-188 (40x40); app/(tabs)/list.tsx:33-38 (36x36); app/user/[id].tsx:157-162 (22pt icon + hitSlop 8 = 38x38); app/spot/[id].tsx:194-205 (40pt tall row)
findings.reproduction: Feed → tap a move card → tap the round back arrow floating at the top-left over the hero image (40x40). Join that move → scroll to Move chat → type a message → tap the round orange send arrow (40x40). Feed tab → tap the map icon at top-right of the header (36x36). Any user profile → tap the "…" at top-right (38x38 including its hitSlop).
findings.consequence: Explicit dimensions, no arithmetic needed — these are declared as `width: 40, height: 40` (move/[id].tsx:392, spot/[id].tsx:256, MoveChat.tsx:179) and `width: 36, height: 36` (list.tsx:35). All are 4-8pt short of 44 with no hitSlop. app/user/[id].tsx:157 is the ONLY control in the entire codebase that sets hitSlop, and it is undersized: `<Ionicons size={22}>` + `hitSlop={{top:8,bottom:8,left:8,right:8}}` = 22 + 16 = 38x38, still 6pt short on both axes — and it is the entry point to the block/report menu (openSafetyMenu at line 22). The two detail-screen back buttons are the only visible exit from full-screen routes (headerShown:false at app/_layout.tsx:53); on Android, where native-stack does not enable an edge-swipe-back gesture by default, a missed tap on that 40pt circle leaves only the hardware back key. spot/[id].tsx:194 ("Dropped by" → user profile) has no padding at all: its height is its tallest child, `<Avatar size={40}>`, so 40pt.

findings.title: Activity empty-state "Create a move" button computes to ~41pt tall
findings.reproduction: Sign in as a brand-new account with no notifications → Activity tab → the "All clear" empty state → tap the orange "Create a move" button.
findings.consequence: Arithmetic: paddingVertical 12*2 = 24 + label fontSize 14 with no lineHeight override. At the iOS SF Pro default metric (~1.2x) that is 16.8pt → 40.8pt total; at Android Roboto's ~1.17x it is 40.4pt. Marked HYPOTHESIS rather than CONFIRMED because this one sits close enough to the boundary that the exact font metric decides it: at a 1.4x line box the total reaches 43.6pt and at 1.45x it clears 44. Under the standard metrics it is 3pt short, with no hitSlop. Consequence is mild — it is a convenience shortcut on an empty screen, and the Create tab button (52x52 inside an 80pt tab bar) does the same thing — but it is the empty state's only call to action for a new user.
